title: SRAM cell (6T)
summary: A 6-transistor (6T) SRAM cell stores 1 bit. Structure: two cross-coupled inverters (4 transistors: 2 PMOS + 2 NMOS) forming a bistable latch, plus two access transistors (NMOS) controlled by the word line. Bit lines (BL, BL_bar) are used for read/write. Read: precharge BL/BL_bar, assert word line, sense differential. Write: drive BL/BL_bar to the desired value, assert word line.

structure.meaning: 2 cross-coupled CMOS inverters (2 PMOS + 2 NMOS). Bistable: holds 0 or 1.
Connect the cell to bit lines (BL, BL_bar) when word line is asserted.
Controls access transistors. Asserted to read/write.
Differential pair for read (sense) and write (drive).
Precharge BL/BL_bar to VDD, assert WL, sense the differential. Cell must not flip (read stability).
Drive BL to desired value, BL_bar to complement, assert WL. Cell flips to new value.
Cell ratio (pull-down vs access transistor strength) must ensure read doesn't flip the cell.
Access transistor must be strong enough to overpower the inverter during write.

notes: 6T SRAM is the standard for L1/L2/L3 caches (fast, but large area).
8T SRAM (6T + 2 read transistors) improves read stability for low voltage.
SRAM is volatile (loses data when power is off).
SRAM density: ~1 transistor per bit (6T cell = 6 transistors per bit).
